conflicts.reason: Nintendo of Europe's born-digital spec page (1.1 kg) over an OCR reading of the Japanese manual scan (約 880g) whose neighbouring width figure is visibly mis-read; the gap may also be a regional or included-part difference neither source explains.

notes: Nintendo of Europe 'Nintendo History' Technical Details page; axes labelled by Nintendo (Width, Depth, Height), so body.width=260, body.depth=190, body.height=73 as printed. The page does not say whether projecting parts are excluded: excludes_projections null. Mass 1.1 kg as printed, recorded as 1100 g (decimal shift; the page's 2.42 lb is its own conversion).

MASS CONFLICT: the scan of the Japanese NINTENDO64 (NUS-001(JPN)) instruction manual (archive.org item nintendo-64-manual-japan-600dpi-ozidual, Japanese OCR text layer) prints '約 880g' in its 仕様 block; the same block's width is OCR-garbled ('幅 e60mmx 奥 行き 190mmx 高 さ 73mm'), which agrees with Nintendo of Europe on depth and height. Both masses are in conflicts[]; Nintendo of Europe's born-digital 1.1 kg is kept, the 880 g OCR figure is flagged for a human check of the scan.

media/ports/controls: scan of Nintendo of America's Nintendo 64 Control Deck instruction booklet (archive.org item nintendo64-manual, print code NUS-S-HB-USA-4); quotes are the scan's OCR text layer, clean lines. 'Nintendo 64 Components': Game Pak Slot; 'Load a Nintendo 64 Game Pak into the top of the Control Deck' → cartridge_top 1. Ports: Controller Sockets 1-4 → controller_proprietary 4; Memory Expansion (top, Jumper Pak) and Expansion Connector (on bottom) → expansion 2; AC Power Supply Connection Port → power_in 1; Multi Out Connector → multi_av_out 1. The components list as OCR'd does not show the power switch or reset labels; they are sourced from the booklet's operating steps ('Slide the N64 Power Switch', 'Reset button') → power_switch 1, reset_button 1.
The AC Power Supply plugs into the rear port 'with the triangle on top'; its connector form is not named, so features.power_inlet stays null.
